title: Grid Sizing
summary: Covers every way to size grid tracks: fixed units, auto, fr, minmax(), repeat(), the grid-template shorthand, and implicit tracks via grid-auto-rows/columns. Also shows Chrome DevTools' grid overlay and finishes with an exercise that reproduces a responsive grid.

concepts.heading: Fixed-size tracks
points: grid-template-rows: 100px 200px and grid-template-columns: 400px 800px create exactly those track sizes. With four items you get a 2x2 grid.
Fixed tracks are not responsive: resizing the window does not change them.
rem also counts as fixed for this purpose. It scales with the root font size but not with the viewport.

grid-template is a shorthand: rows first, a slash, then columns, e.g. grid-template: 100px 200px / 400px 800px. It is compact but hides intent, so prefer the explicit longhands while learning; you will still meet it in other people's code.

concepts.heading: auto tracks
points: A column set to auto stretches to use the remaining horizontal space of the container (the grid fills 100% of the available width). With 200px auto, the second column grows and shrinks with the window.
A row set to auto behaves differently: it only becomes as tall as its content and does not follow the viewport height.
So auto on columns = fill available space; auto on rows = fit content.

concepts.heading: Fractional units (fr)
points: fr tracks share the available space in ratio, e.g. 1fr 2fr gives the second track double the first. Decimals and other ratios such as 2.5fr or 3fr 5fr are fine.
Columns use the available width; rows follow content height. If you add more content to one cell, its fr row grows and the others adjust to keep the ratio.
(Extra) Before fr ratios are applied, fixed-size tracks are subtracted from the container's free space.

concepts.heading: minmax()
points: minmax(min, max) lets a track flex within limits. For example a column of minmax(400px, 800px) shrinks as far as 400px and grows up to 800px, then stops. Useful to stop images or text blocks from becoming too narrow or too wide.
(Extra) The repo demo uses minmax(400px, 5fr), mixing a length and an fr value, which is also valid.

concepts.heading: repeat()
points: repeat(count, size) removes repetition: repeat(8, 1fr) replaces eight copies of 1fr, and repeat(2, 200px) replaces 200px 200px.
It produces the same layout as listing each track by hand.

concepts.heading: Explicit versus implicit tracks
points: Items fill cells left to right, then continue on the next row, starting at the top-left.
A template larger than the number of items just leaves empty cells at the end (a 2x3 grid with four items leaves two cells empty).
If there are more items than the template provides, extra items go into automatically created tracks. New rows are as tall as their content; they reuse the existing column widths.
grid-auto-rows and grid-auto-columns set the size of these automatically created tracks, e.g. grid-auto-rows: 300px. Handy when items are added dynamically.

concepts.heading: Chrome DevTools grid overlay
points: Open DevTools (right-click, Inspect, or the three-dot menu, More tools). Elements with display: grid show a 'grid' badge in the Elements panel; clicking it toggles an overlay.
The Layout tab lets you change the overlay colour and toggle line numbers, track sizes and extended lines.
Overlay track-size labels show the real size of each column and row, which helps to debug sizing.

task.name: Grid Sizing test: match the green grid
task.starting_point: The 'Test' page of the course's grid-sizing demo site: a CSS text box with 'Apply CSS', a green target grid (.parent) and a purple grid you control. Size hints are written in the cells. Only CSS for the grid container may be written.
task.goal: Make the purple grid look and resize like the green one.
steps: Set display: grid on the container.
Rows: the first two are equal and the third is twice as tall, so grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr 2fr.
Columns: first expands to fill space (auto), second is fixed (400px), third has limits (minmax(200px, 500px)).
The extra last row is 50px high; set grid-auto-rows: 50px rather than adding a fourth explicit row.
Click Apply CSS, then resize the window to check the responsive behaviour matches. If nothing works, check spelling, e.g. the 's' in grid-template-rows and -columns.
task.expected_result: Same layout as the green grid at any width: first column flexes, second stays 400px, third flexes between 200 and 500px; the fourth row stays 50px.

pitfalls: Typos such as grid-template-row (missing s); the property is silently ignored.
Expecting auto rows to fill the viewport height; they only fit content.
Assuming rem-sized tracks respond to viewport size.
Defining too few explicit tracks and being surprised by content-sized implicit rows; set grid-auto-rows.
(Extra) The repo's footers ('Made with ...') are not part of the lesson.

playground.coverage: Blurb lists fixed, fr, auto and minmax tracks. Tasks cover 2x2 with a 1:2 ratio, repeat(2, 200px) plus grid-auto-rows: 300px with a fifth item, and 200px minmax(400px, 5fr) with a draggable preview width.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the grid-template shorthand (rows / columns) with a note on why the longhand is clearer.
Explain auto on columns versus rows explicitly, with a live demo showing rows not following the window height.

Add the match-the-green-grid exercise (1fr 1fr 2fr / auto 400px minmax(200px, 500px) / grid-auto-rows 50px) with a target grid and Apply CSS box.
Explore-demo idea: item-count slider plus column/row count inputs to show empty cells and implicit rows, with grid-auto-rows toggle.
Add spelling pitfall note (grid-template-rows needs the final s).
